title: CS intake: enterprise asks aggregation scorer and initial scoper
creator: Avery Chen
description: Create a lightweight, repeatable process and scoring rubric for Sales/CS to aggregate multiple enterprise feature requests (non-bug) and produce an initial scoping artifact suitable for PM prioritization and engineering intake. The goal is to reduce back-and-forth with Sales/CS, accelerate discovery for high-value customers, and produce consistent artifacts (one-pagers + initial impact/effort scores) that feed into the product intake pipeline.
outcome_summary: Deliver a one-page aggregation template, a 5-factor scoring rubric (value, complexity, regulatory scope, data sensitivity, strategic alignment), and a short training doc for CS to create initial scoping bundles. Integrate with existing Linear intake flow so high-scoring bundles are auto-surfaced to PMs and trigger a 2-week discovery slot when approved.
acceptance_criteria: CS can produce a consolidated enterprise-ask bundle in under 48 hours using the template
Each bundle contains: customer context, example use cases, 1-3 required acceptance criteria, suggested priority score, and suggested initial release window
Scoring rubric maps to automated labels in Linear and surfaces >P1 bundles to a PM triage dashboard
Onboarded 2 pilot CS reps and validated rubric on 5 live enterprise requests with feedback cycle recorded
Documented handoff checklist for engineering discovery with required artifacts and gating questions
scope_notes: Scope limited to non-bug feature asks from Sales/CS. Does not include SSO/legal contract negotiations or billing changes. Initial phase focuses on highest ARR accounts and seats in NA/EU. Post-launch phase will broaden to APAC and lighter-touch accounts.
triage_rubric: Proposed 5-factor scoring: 1) Customer ARR/strategic value (0-5), 2) Product fit / feature reuse potential (0-5), 3) Engineering complexity estimate (T-shirt: S/M/L mapped to 0-5), 4) Privacy/regulatory surface (0-5), 5) Time-to-value / integration effort (0-5). Sum => 0-25. Thresholds: 18+ = PM fast-track, 12-17 = Backlog review, <12 = CS nurture.
initial_workflow: 1) CS creates enterprise bundle using template and scores it; 2) Bundle auto-creates Linear ticket with PM-assign label and rubric metadata; 3) PM triage within 3 business days; 4) If fast-track, schedule 2-week discovery with Eng/Design; 5) If backlog, assign to product backlog with suggested milestone.
notes_on_tradeoffs: We prioritize speed of CS submission over exhaustive technical detail; the intent is to surface product-level value quickly. Tradeoff: more false positives that PMs must triage. To mitigate, require one supporting artifact (customer screenshot, workflow, Slack thread) and customer contact for PO clarity.
pilot_plan: Pilot with 2 CS reps and 4 enterprise accounts over 4 weeks. Measure: time-to-bundle, PM triage time, conversion to discovery, accuracy of initial complexity estimate against engineering estimate.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: CS scores are inconsistent -> Mitigation: short calibration sessions and example bundles
Risk: engineering overloaded by false fast-tracks -> Mitigation: strict threshold and weekly review cadence
Risk: missing security/compliance details -> Mitigation: add mandatory checkbox for 'has regulated data' to surface to Security early
